facts.fact_text: At the material time, the applicant was deputy chairman of the Youth Committee of an opposition party called Musavat.
A demonstration was planned to be held on 2 April 2011 in Baku.
A demonstration was planned to be held on 20 October 2012 in Baku.
The applicant attended the demonstration on 2 April 2011.
The applicant attended the demonstration on 20 October 2012.
The Baku City Executive Authority refused to authorise the demonstrations at the places indicated by the organisers.
Shortly after the demonstration on 2 April 2011 had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
Shortly after the demonstration on 20 October 2012 had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation at the demonstration on 2 April 2011.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation at the demonstration on 20 October 2012.

The administrative offence report issued on 2 April 2011 stated that by deliberately failing to comply with a lawful order of the police, the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The administrative offence report issued on 20 October 2012 stated that by deliberately failing to comply with a lawful order of the police, the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 2 April 2011, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that an individual who is subject to administrative offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity shall be given an opportunity to familiarise himself with the administrative offence report.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 2 April 2011, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that an individual who is subject to administrative offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity has the right to a copy of the administrative offence report.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants in the demonstrations were demanding free and fair elections in Azerbaijan.
The participants in the demonstrations were demanding democratic reforms in Azerbaijan.
The Baku City Executive Authority refused to authorise the demonstrations at the places indicated by the organisers.
In the first case (arrest on 2 April 2011), the applicant was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest.
In the first case (arrest on 2 April 2011), the applicant was not given access to a lawyer while he was in police custody.
In the second case (arrest on 20 October 2012), the applicant was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest.
In the second case (arrest on 20 October 2012), the applicant was not given access to a lawyer while he was in police custody.
According to the applicant, he was never served with copies of the administrative offence reports from his case files.
According to the applicant, he was never served with other documents from his case files.
